title: Scientists Warn of Hidden Negative Effect of Vitamin D Supplement
seoTitle: Hidden negative effect of vitamin D supplement
subtitle: Research shows that intake of vitamin D2 can lower the body's vitamin D3 levels.
excerpt: Scientists warn that the popular vitamin D2 supplement may reduce vitamin D3, the most effective form produced by sunlight.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
The role of vitamin D in the body

Vitamin D plays an important role in maintaining human health. Traditionally, the human body obtains this nutrient through direct sun exposure and the consumption of certain foods. However, when natural synthesis is insufficient, many people turn to dietary supplements to keep levels adequate.

Vitamin D supplements are widely available on the market and are used by many segments of the population. Yet science shows that these products are not all the same, varying in composition and in the impacts they have on the human body.

The discovery about vitamin D2 and vitamin D3

Scientists have issued an important alert about a popular type of vitamin D supplement that may have a hidden downside. According to new research, a common form of this supplement can produce an unwanted and unexpected effect in the body.

Researchers found that ingesting vitamin D2 can actually reduce the levels of vitamin D3 in the body. Vitamin D3 is the form naturally produced by sunlight exposure and is considered more effective at raising overall vitamin D levels in humans.

Impacts on the immune system

The difference between supplement forms can also influence the body's defensive capacity. Earlier studies suggest that vitamin D3 may offer stronger immune protection against invading agents such as viruses and bacteria.

The immune system relies on many factors to function properly, and the presence of specific nutrients is one of its pillars for bodily protection. In light of these findings, the choice of supplement type becomes a relevant factor to ensure expected benefits are achieved without compromising the levels of other essential forms of the nutrient in the body.

With information from ScienceDaily.
